mechanism_narrative: A steady rise in WORKPLACES mobility indicates more employees returning to offices, which increases weekday foot traffic and discretionary spending near workplaces, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -39.6 to -30.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to rise but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises above -12, it signals that panic-buying has subsided and households are shifting spending toward discretionary retail, driving RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -16.4 to -10.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above -12 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility signifies a broad return to pre-pandemic commuting and leisure travel, which together amplify retail footfall more than either series alone, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by >5 points over 4 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -71.3 to -68.1 and WORKPLACES from -39.6 to -30.4
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by >5 points over 4 weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 4 weeks, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime with declining residential mobility, an increase in PARKS activity signals that residents are resuming outdoor leisure, which spills over into nearby retail and recreation spending, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose to -17.1 while RESIDENTIAL fell to 16.6 in the last week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL declines in a reopening regime but RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility above 15 reflects continued work-from-home behavior, which reduces trips to retail and recreation venues and keeps RETAIL_REC depressed over the next week.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 15 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC rises over the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal transition to spring in Melbourne increases outdoor recreation and park visits, which historically coincide with higher retail and recreation mobility as consumers combine outdoor trips with shopping, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved to -17.1 in t-0w from -28.1 in t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS rises during the spring transition but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks, the seasonal hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week improvement in GROCERY_PHARM mobility of more than 3 points indicates reduced stockpiling and greater household mobility, which immediately frees up time and inclination for discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved by 2.7 points from t-1w to t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved by 2.7 points
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM improves by >3 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening restrictions regime, a drop in TRANSIT mobility below -75 signals renewed stay-at-home orders that suppress all non-essential travel, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is at -68.1 in t-0w, above the -75 threshold
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below -75 but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
